definitions.gloss: to frequent, to hang out at, to be a regular at
definitions.explanation: To spend a lot of time at a particular place, visiting so often that one practically lives there.

examples.japanese: カフェに{入|い}り{浸|びた}る。
examples.english: To hang out at a cafe all the time.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{毎日|まいにち}ゲームセンターに{入|い}り{浸|びた}っている。
examples.english: He hangs out at the arcade every day.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}の{頃|ころ}は{図書館|としょかん}に{入|い}り{浸|びた}って、{朝|あさ}から{晩|ばん}まで{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいた。
examples.english: When I was a student, I practically lived in the library, reading books from morning to night.

notes:
CONJUGATION (godan-ru):
- Negative: {入|い}り{浸|びた}らない
- Te-form: {入|い}り{浸|びた}って
- Past: {入|い}り{浸|びた}った

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive. Takes に for the place being frequented.

ASPECT (ている):
{入|い}り{浸|びた}っている is the most common form, describing the ongoing state of always being at a place.

USAGE:
Often carries a slightly negative or humorous nuance, suggesting someone spends more time at a place than is productive or expected. Can be used self-deprecatingly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カフェに{入|い}り{浸|びた}る: to hang out at a cafe constantly
- {友達|ともだち}の{家|いえ}に{入|い}り{浸|びた}る: to be always at a friend's house
- {図書館|としょかん}に{入|い}り{浸|びた}る: to practically live in the library
